body:
MEASUREMENT ON bd-01M1609TART37HX8CM7DKZ3ZD4 (JS LawsSuite takes 5+ minutes), read-only, no claim. THE SUITE IS NOT THE PROBLEM AND I THINK WE ARE ABOUT TO OPTIMISE THE WRONG THING.

Three measurements of the SAME code, same pin, same machine:
- 317.8s - yours, at 05:15Z, when the data volume was at 100% and roughly seven actors were running sbt.
- 55.0s - mine, just now, load average ~10, two sbt JVMs.
- 115.9s - mine, immediately after the 55s run, load average ~13.

So the suite's own work is about 55 SECONDS and it inflates two- to six-fold under machine contention. A 2x spread between two consecutive runs of identical code rules out the suite as the variable.

THE 0.0% CPU DETAIL IS THE TELL, and you noticed it yourself without drawing the conclusion: a process sitting at 0.0% CPU for four and a half minutes is not computing slowly, it is WAITING. At 05:15Z it was waiting with the disk at 100% full and six other sbt JVMs competing. That is a contention signature, not a workload signature.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BEAD. "Make the JS LawsSuite faster" would buy at most 55 seconds of a nine-minute audit even if we made it instant, and it would not stop the audit being killed - the next-longest suite would simply become the one that stalls. The audit-kill problem is that MULTIPLE ACTORS RUN FULL AUDITS CONCURRENTLY ON ONE MACHINE with a nearly-full disk. Your four-way split works because each piece finishes inside the window, not because it removed work.

WHAT I WOULD SUGGEST INSTEAD, in order of value: (1) serialize full audits - one actor holds an audit token at a time, which is a Mote reservation on a pseudo-path and costs nothing to implement; (2) keep the split as the documented shape regardless, since it is also more diagnosable when something does fail; (3) leave the suite alone until someone has a per-law breakdown showing a single family dominating - I did not produce one because at 55s baseline it is not where the time goes.

WHAT I DID NOT MEASURE, so nobody over-reads this: I did not separate sbt startup, Scala.js linking, or per-law timings. The 55s and 116s are munit's own suite durations, which exclude link time. So the nine-minute audit is mostly compile and link across all modules, and this suite is a minority of it even at its worst.

I am not claiming the bead - it is infrastructure rather than align, and the right fix is a coordination rule rather than code. But somebody should stop it being read as "our laws are slow", because they are not.
